Description: A fierce couple’s argument in the Billiard room reveals a strained engagement and, through mentions of Tony Dauer and other family members, exposes deeper emotional and family conflict. It ends with Person No. 10 storming out in an emotional breakdown and the front door being knocked.
Location: Billiard room (Billiard room)
Key Information:
  - Piano music can be heard from another room.
  - There is a clear engagement relationship between Person No. 6 and Person No. 10.
  - The core of the conflict revolves around being neglected, jealousy, a third party, and family relationships.
  - Person No. 10 displays obvious drunkenness and emotional instability during the conversation.
  - Tony Dauer is mentioned as a family member and comparison target to intensify the argument.
  - The argument is forcibly interrupted after an external event occurs (the front door being knocked).
Characters:
  [Edmund Galley (Edmund Galley)] One of the villa’s hosts; Person No. 10’s fiancé.
    · Repeatedly attempts to de-escalate and end the conversation during the argument.
    · Proposes returning to the Living room to avoid further conflict.
    · Shows concern about Person No. 10’s drinking state.
    · Displays obvious anxiety and regret after Person No. 10 leaves.
  [Eve Dauer (Eve Dauer)] Person No. 6’s fiancée, highly emotionally unstable.
    · Explicitly mentions her engagement to Person No. 6.
    · Accuses Person No. 6 of ignoring her and still having feelings for other women.
    · Repeatedly focuses the conflict on a third party and being sidelined.
    · Leaves the Billiard room after completely losing control, accompanied by destructive behavior.
  [Tony Dauer (Dauer)] Person No. 4, a mentioned family member and Person No. 10’s younger brother. Based on the naming rules, this can be identified as Tony Dauer.
    · Is mentioned by Person No. 6 in a contemptuous tone, saying he joined the army just for fun.
    · Appears as a comparison target and emotional trigger in the argument.
    · Does not appear in this scene, but holds an important position in character relationships and family structure.
